accounting: Organize programs for downstream hierarchical work-remaining accounting. A program is a durable work-policy package, not merely a topic, method, result, or submission. Create the smallest accounting tree sufficient for future contribution attribution. Split work when credible future contributions could independently activate, stop, solve, prune, or materially change the remaining work of one package without the other. Do not split merely because a submission contains multiple claims, methods, computations, or intermediate results. When several separately estimable work packages directly advance the same narrower objective, create or reuse that objective as their parent and place the packages beneath it. The parent retains only genuine integration or coordination work. Place a program beneath the narrowest existing program whose objective it directly advances. Do not infer accounting ancestry solely from mathematical or evidentiary dependency. Preserve existing topology when a later submission strengthens, reproduces, or supplies additional evidence for an existing work package. Do not automatically create unstructured-search nodes, unary grouping programs, or one program per intermediate result. Use these principles only to organize topology; do not estimate probabilities, hours, remaining work, or credit. In topologyRationale, state the shared activation event represented by each new parent, what could make sibling packages activate, stop, or change separately, and why apparently distinct material was consolidated.
candidate: Apply four additional controls. First, choose program boundaries using an author-blind intervention test. Split two work packages only when plausible future accepted evidence could change the continue, stop, solve, or prune decision for one without changing the other, regardless of who submitted the current evidence; never create boundaries to maximize attributable credit. A grouping parent must be the narrowest genuine shared activation gate and materially narrower than its current parent. Root is not an adequate substitute when siblings share a narrower objective, while a generic umbrella such as broad field progress, theory improvement, or converse strengthening is not a genuine gate if it would absorb independently activated future programs. Place a new program beneath the narrowest existing program whose objective it directly advances. Mathematical or evidentiary reliance on an existing result does not by itself establish accounting ancestry. Second, link an intermediate result only to the narrowest program or programs whose own remaining work it directly changes. Link a parent only when the result directly changes genuine parent-level integration or coordination work, never merely because the owning leaf lies beneath that parent. A grouping parent normally has no direct result membership. Preserve stable program and result IDs when later accepted evidence strengthens, reproduces, or adds support to the same durable work package or semantic result; do not create submission-shaped duplicates. Third, accepted claim assessments jointly control every output surface, including program titles, objectives, summaries, residuals, placementAudit, topologyRationale, result statements, and qualifications. Scope qualifications limit any stronger-looking declared statement. When accepted assessment surfaces differ in strength, emit their weaker intersection everywhere, preserving modal and quantifier force. If accepted scope says a method may succeed or may exclude an object, never rewrite that as can, does, will, succeeds, or excludes; describe residual work as investigating whether it succeeds. Fourth, obey the operation contract on the first response. Every entity ID appears in exactly one operation array. Create a new program or intermediate result once, only in topologyOperations with action create; never repeat it in contentOperations. Use contentOperations for an existing entity whose topology is unchanged. contribution.directProgramIds must equal the union of its results' primaryProgramId and relatedProgramIds. When updating an existing result, refresh its owning existing program and every existing ancestor through root. Use these controls only to organize and synthesize accepted knowledge; do not estimate probabilities, hours, remaining work, deltas, or awards.
